description: Three hook groups. (1) PermissionRequest: carry an attention-store answer into a live permission prompt, so a manager can relay the operator's decision without the operator opening the worker's tab. Fail-open: an unanswered prompt stays for the human. Kill switch: SUPERVISOR_PERMISSION_POLL=off. (2) PreToolUse on AskUserQuestion: deny a MANAGER session's menu when an option offers a manager-owned action (open / resume / ready / file / repair) as a choice, naming the action to execute instead — a rule relayed by SendMessage does not hold (measured 2026-10-15: a manager reverted to a menu within ~2 hours of being told), so only a deny keeps the gate. Scoped to managers by fleet-board.py's rule 1 (name resolves to a 23 Topics / 24 Goals page, or colour is orange), computed locally — never by calling fleet-board.py, whose measured 14-73 s per call would stall the very tool this polices. Fail-open: any parse error, a missing session_id, an unreadable registry entry, an unresolvable vault or a non-manager session allows the call — a gate that failed closed on a parse error would block every AskUserQuestion in every session that loads this plugin. Kill switch: SUPERVISOR_MANAGER_MENU_GUARD=off. (3) UserPromptSubmit / Stop / Notification / SessionEnd: record what the session is doing, so the heartbeat timer can carry it onto the stamp the attention store reads. Fail-open: a missed write costs a stale state for up to one 30 s tick. Kill switch: SUPERVISOR_HEARTBEAT_STATE=off — without one, the only way to stop four python3 spawns per turn on every session on the machine is to edit this manifest. NOTE: the Notification mapping is ANY notification -> waiting-on-operator, not a 1:1 park mapping — Claude Code also emits notifications for non-park events (idle-prompt nudges, task completion). Over-reporting a park is the safe direction, and the state is only read as a description rather than as a gate. NOTE: SessionEnd CLEARS the record rather than writing one, because this fires for every session on the machine and nothing else unlinks a record; a SIGKILLed session still leaves one behind, which is a known and accepted gap.
